title: Printed always, sometimes, never cards
subject: Mathematics
unit: Summer 1: Shape; position and direction; decimals
source: Seeded from mathematics/y5 lesson 70 (Printed always, sometimes, never cards)
intro: Lesson 70: Reasoning about 2-D shapes. To understand how to reason about the properties of 2-D shapes

blocks.title: Sort into: Always / Sometimes / Never
blocks.task: sort them into the columns: Always, Sometimes, Never.
blocks.answer: Always: A square is a rectangle; A rectangle has equal diagonals. Sometimes: A pentagon is regular. Never: A triangle has 2 right angles

cards:
counter-example
one example that shows a
statement is false
blocks.task: use them to test yourself or a partner.

questions.q: 'A triangle can have an obtuse angle.' Always, sometimes or never?
questions.model: Teacher draws one with 120° and one with all acute angles: sometimes.

questions.q: Always, sometimes or never: a parallelogram has right angles; a kite has 2 pairs of equal sides; a trapezium has a right angle
questions.a: Sometimes; always (two pairs of equal adjacent sides); sometimes
questions.model: Teacher: a rectangle is a parallelogram with right angles, a rhombus may not have them: sometimes.

questions.q: Write your own 'sometimes' statement about quadrilaterals with one example of each.
questions.a: For example 'a quadrilateral has parallel sides': yes for a rectangle, no for a kite

questions.q: Prove false with a counter-example: 'All shapes with 4 right angles are squares.'
'A square has 4 lines of symmetry.' A) always B) sometimes C) never
Big question: how do we decide?
questions.a: Test examples; one counter-example shows a statement is not always true
